system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

[ON-PICKERING-2020#0074] Investigation into the emergency alerts sent on January 12, 2020 (Box 1: Planned maintenance outage at Pickering Nuclear Generating Station):
Box 1: Planned maintenance outage at Pickering Nuclear Generating Station On January 12, 2020, Unit 1 at Pickering Nuclear Generating Station was on a planned maintenance outage and was therefore out of service in a shutdown position. At 1:21 am, there was a momentary loss of power to some equipment on this Unit resulting in an internal notification. OPG provided a courtesy update to the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) regarding this loss of power.

[ON-PICKERING-2020#0106] Investigation into the emergency alerts sent on January 12, 2020 (Findings):
Findings The PEOC only maintained templates with pre-scripted messaging for nuclear alerts. The PNERP required that nuclear emergency bulletins be pre-scripted for each reactor facility and notification category, as far as practical. The alert issued in error included a pre-scripted template maintained by the PEOC for the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station.

data.summary: The English text can be delivered: 516 GSM-7 characters across 6 pages, well under the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, and no languages are required by the GENERIC profile. However, the first GSM-7 page (about 93 characters) holds only the preamble 'This is a Province of Ontario emergency bulletin which applies to people within ten (10) kilometres of the…'. It carries neither the hazard (the incident at Pickering) nor the action (no protective action needed). Pages can be scheduled and displayed independently, so a reader who sees only page 1 learns of a nuclear bulletin with no hazard or action. That is a fixable drafting issue.

objections.issue: The first page carries neither the hazard nor the action. The opening ~93 GSM-7 characters are spent on the issuing authority and the 10 km applicability boundary. The incident statement and the 'DO NOT need to take any protective actions' instruction do not appear until pages 2–4. Multipage cell broadcast pages are handled independently, so the first page must stand on its own. Here it would show a nuclear bulletin with no hazard or action, which risks alarm or misreading.
objections.fix: Reorder so that page 1 (the first ~90 characters) states the hazard and the action together, for example: 'Pickering Nuclear incident: NO radiation release. NO action needed by public. Ontario emergency bulletin.' Then put the 10 km applicability, the responder details and 'stay tuned to local media' on later pages. Keep the total under 15 pages in GSM-7.

no_basis.concern: The wording closely matches the pre-scripted Pickering template that was issued in error on January 12, 2020. Whether this bulletin should be broadcast at all, given it advises no action, is a decision for people and is outside the deliverability mandate. No clause shown supports objecting on that basis.
